Work History

Atlas Branch Manager

Role
Design Systems Lead
Organization
Experian
Platforms
Figma Plugin

Context

Atlas Branch Manager is a Figma plugin I created to manage many concurrent branches across component-library files and contributors. Each branch represents a discrete piece of work, usually tied to Jira.

Platform-agnostic changes can produce separate Web, iOS, and Android tickets across different Jira boards. Keeping roughly sixteen branches—and more in other libraries—in memory created heavy cognitive load and repeated context switching.

Large library files also made opening every branch slow, while manually searching separate Jira boards made it difficult to know what was in flight, who was working, and when a branch was safe to merge.

Approach

One view of the work

The plugin centralizes branches in a Kanban-style view with statuses such as Design in progress, Ready for development, Development in progress, and Done. Color-coded ticket statuses, active and completed summaries, branch creation information, creator, and last editor give each item enough context to scan without opening every file.

Ticket associations

It searches Jira by branch name to associate relevant tickets automatically. Designers can review the matches and detach tickets when an association is incorrect.

Connected navigation

Search, domain filtering, sorting, refresh, and direct open controls make it easier to move from a status check into the relevant Figma branch. Settings support the connected Figma, Jira, and Confluence workflow, including file connections, organizational domains, search roots, and Jira integration.

Adoption

A shared operating view

Atlas Branch Manager keeps component-library work visible across design, development, and the related Jira workflow, giving contributors a common view of what is in flight and ready for the next step.

Outcomes

Lower cognitive load

Branches, contributors, tickets, and status context are visible together instead of requiring repeated memory checks across files and boards.

Faster status checks

Once related tickets are done, I can see that immediately, open the branch directly, and make a more confident merge decision.

Less context switching

The tool reduces the need to reopen large library files or search multiple Jira boards just to understand what is ready for the next step.

Now

Names still matter

Automatic ticket association depends on useful branch naming. Designers can review and detach incorrect matches rather than treating the association as authoritative.

Visibility is not automation

The plugin improves visibility and navigation, but it does not replace the underlying Jira and Figma workflow or the judgment required to merge work safely.

Built around the real load

The product decision came from the operational reality of many concurrent branches and contributors, not from adding another dashboard for its own sake. Atlas Branch Manager remains a practical way to manage that visibility across design, development, and the related Jira workflow.
